meanings.note: High-frequency Russian expressive spoken interjection meaning 'oh', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh, look!
Oh, sorry.
Oh, look! The news.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That's mine.
And this is for you.
And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
And does the governor support you?

examples.text: Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'cinema, movies, film' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Then invite me to the movies.
So, let's look at the schedule in the cinema.

examples.text: Зачем ты вообще ведёшь её в кино?
examples.trans: Why are you even taking her to the movies?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

examples.trans: A new house.
I need a new job.

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'role, part' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Он сыграл главную роль в спектакле.
examples.trans: He played the lead role in the play.

examples.text: Ладно, я попробую сыграть эту роль.
examples.trans: Okay, I will try to play this role.
Everyone plays roles.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('necessary, needed').

examples.trans: I need a job too.
Do you need a pen?
He needs money.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
I'm doing my homework.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'so, then; like that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
That's good like that.
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

подумать.gloss: to think (for a while), to think it over

meanings.en: to think (for a while), to think it over
meanings.note: Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'умать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to think (for a while), to think it over', paired with 'думать'.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
I've been thinking.
Think again.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'for; behind', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you for your trust!
Thanks for the present.
What for?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'movie, film' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я всегда смотрел фильмы про войну.
examples.trans: I always watched movies about the war.
An interesting film.
I love romantic movies.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nothing', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: There's nothing left.
I don't know anything.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Chef, I didn't take it.
I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

examples.trans: I didn't understand.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?
I understand you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'обще').

examples.trans: That's no problem at all.
I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'our, ours', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'junk, stuff' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is not our usual trash.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое барахло.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new junk.

представить.gloss: to imagine, to picture; to introduce

meanings.en: to imagine, to picture; to introduce
meanings.note: Prefix 'пред-' ('before, fore-') indicates anticipation or prior position (stem 'ставить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to imagine, to picture; to introduce', paired with 'представлять'.

examples.text: Представь: тебе сорок лет, жена красавица.
examples.trans: Imagine: you're forty, with a beautiful wife.

examples.text: Представь: тебе сорок лет, жена красавица, дети, бизнес. А тебя все зовут врунишкой!
examples.trans: Imagine: you're forty, with a beautiful wife, children, a business. And everyone still calls you a little liar!

examples.text: Представь: тебе сорок лет, жена красавица, дети, бизнес.
examples.trans: Imagine: you're forty, with a beautiful wife, children, a business.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'допад'). Common masculine noun meaning 'waterfall' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Picture a waterfall.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новый водопад.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new waterfall.

лежать.gloss: to lie, to be lying down

meanings.en: to lie, to be lying down
meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to lie, to be lying down', paired with 'полежать'.

examples.trans: But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.
The book is lying on the table.

examples.text: Телевизор мне смотреть недолго. А с Гришкой лежать вечность.
examples.trans: I won't be watching TV for much longer. But I'll be lying next to Grishka for eternity.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'on, onto; for', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'edge, side, rim; region' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Over there, you see, she's warming up on the side.

examples.text: Дом стоит на самом краю деревни.
examples.trans: The house stands at the very edge of the village.

examples.text: Здравствуйте. Вон, видите, с краю разминается.
examples.trans: Hello. Over there, you see, she's warming up on the side.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'raft' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They built a sturdy raft.

examples.text: Он посадил меня на этот плот один.
examples.trans: He placed me onto this raft alone.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Oh yeah?
Yes, it's me.
Oh yeah? When?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('cold, chilly; distant').

examples.trans: Cold vodka.
You are a good woman. Cold.

examples.text: Лёня быстро бросил в холодную воду поддон.
examples.trans: Lyonya quickly threw a wooden pallet into cold water.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'wind' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The wind blows from here.
There is a strong wind outside.

examples.text: Конечно, вкусно! Это мой шашлык пахнет, ветер отсюда.
examples.trans: Of course it's delicious! That's my shashlik smelling, the wind is from here.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share with everyone.
I'm with Dad.
Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'shore, bank' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: They will sit quietly on the shore.
They walked along the lake shore.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'which, who', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

examples.text: Чтобы он вернул деньги, которые украл.
examples.trans: For him to give back the money he stole.

examples.text: Который ему город подарил! И откуда у Аллы Евгеньевны новая шуба!
examples.trans: Which the city donated to him! And where Alla Yevgenyevna got a new fur coat!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'already', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been mayor for four years now.
Dad is already home.
I'm already home.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'never', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я никогда не был на море.
examples.trans: I've never been to the sea.
No! Never!

examples.text: Я своему ребёнку никогда не вру.
examples.trans: I never lie to my child.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'affect' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это сокращение тебя точно не коснётся.
examples.trans: This downsizing will definitely not affect you.

examples.text: Нам надо уволить одного лишнего повара.
examples.trans: We need to fire one extra cook.

meanings.note: Common feminine noun meaning 'hand; arm' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Give me your hand.
I shake your hand! (a goodbye)
Right, cheers then.
